data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The checklist is explicitly authored and frozen, whereas the expert's theory is implicit and mutable.","The panel provides redundancy that can catch execution errors, while a single expert has no such redundancy."],"overturn_conditions":["The checklist is shown to be a surface heuristic, not a causal model.","The expert's theory is shown to be causally superior to the checklist."],"shared_structure":["Both domains involve executing a theory (frozen checklist vs internal intuition) against ground truth.","Reliability depends on theory-quality \u00d7 execution-fidelity, not panel-vs-individual."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["Adversarial items that break the observed\u2192latent edge will distinguish causal structure from surface proxy."]},"claim":"A trained non-expert panel using an explicit checklist is more reliable than a single intuition-reliant expert ONLY when the checklist encodes a theory whose causal structure is superior to the expert's working theory. The panel's value is not aggregation (Condorcet) but execution fidelity to a superior frozen theory.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is merely a surface heuristic that tracks the right answer on the evaluated distribution without capturing causal structure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's internal theory is causally superior to the checklist's frozen theory, as in a novel domain the checklist has not caught up to.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel fails to execute the checklist faithfully, introducing noise that overwhelms the fidelity benefit.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Checklist items are observable proxies for latent causes.
